discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological phase, the quantum spin Hall insulator, classified by a Z2 invariant, with protected helical edge states. This revealed that ordinary band insulators come in topologically distinct classes, and it created a new field of quantum matter. Molenkamp and co-workers used carefully engineered HgTe/CdTe quantum wells to observe quantized edge conduction in 2007, and later nonlocal transport, confirming the prediction in a real device. This close interplay of deep theory and clean materials and nanofabrication set off the worldwide study of three-dimensional topological insulators, topological superconductors and Majorana modes, topological semimetals and magnetic topological phases. Topology is now a standard organizing principle of condensed matter physics, and it underlies current efforts toward protected quantum devices.
